_comment: Per-module metadata used by src/components/Modules/ModuleOverview.tsx. Edit freely — no rebuild required after a static-file change; just redeploy. Each entry has: tagline (1 line), description (2-3 sentences), keyFeatures (3-5 bullets), who (audience description), privilege/anyPrivilege (gate identity — used to detect upsell branch), ctaEmail (the address pre-filled when a user clicks 'Talk to your admin').

quiz.label: Quiz
quiz.tagline: Knowledge checks, auto-quiz pools, and topic-wise mastery tracking.
quiz.description: SmartWinnr's knowledge-testing engine. Editors build quizzes — manual, automatic, event-based, or proctored — by pulling questions from a central Question Bank that supports many formats (multiple-choice, fill-in-the-blank, matching, hotspot, drag-and-drop, long/short answer, numeric, and re-order). Questions can include images, audio, or video, and can be organized by topic for easy reuse across campaigns via duplication or bulk import. Editors and managers get detailed reporting — score trends, participation, team comparisons, and question-level breakdowns — to see exactly where knowledge is strong or weak, and whether it's improving over time.
keyFeatures: 8 question types incl. drag-drop and hotspot
Auto-quiz pools with randomised question selection
quiz.who: Authored by Editors. Taken by all Learners. Managers see reportee scores.

smartpath.label: SmartPath
smartpath.tagline: Curated learning journeys that combine quizzes, content, coaching, and live sessions.
smartpath.description: The structured learning-journey builder — essentially a curriculum tool that strings multiple activities (quizzes, SmartFeeds, surveys, coaching, learning sessions, assignments, even external/SCORM content) into one guided path per learner. Editors define the modules and segments in a path and set unlock rules based on completion, score, or time elapsed, so learners move through training in the right order. Paths can be gamified with an attached competition, support instructor-led “Learning Sessions” (classroom or virtual) with attendance tracking, and award a certificate on completion. Reporting covers learner progress, module-level performance, and overall engagement across the full journey.
keyFeatures: Mix quizzes, content, coachings, surveys, and live sessions
Assign by user, group, division, or metatag
smartpath.who: Authored by Editors. Followed by Learners. Managers track reportee progress.

smartfeed.label: SmartFeed
smartfeed.tagline: Bite-sized video and article content delivered to the right audience.
smartfeed.description: A short-form content feed for quick, frequent knowledge nudges. Editors push bite-sized content — videos, images, PDFs, PPTs, audio, or recordings — directly to a team's feed, and can create, edit, resend, or expire posts as needed, targeted to specific groups or teams. Learners can like and comment on feeds, and editors get view/engagement analytics on every post sent, so they know what content is actually landing.
smartfeed.who: Authored by Editors. Consumed by all Learners. Managers see team engagement.

video-coaching.label: Video Coaching
video-coaching.tagline: Submit a recorded pitch, get scored by managers against a rubric.
video-coaching.description: Lets reps submit a recorded pitch or roleplay (video, audio, or screen recording) for a manager to review and score against a defined rubric or set of competencies. Managers can leave written feedback, flag standout submissions as “top videos” so the rest of the team can learn from them, and track submission status across their whole team. This is best suited to real sales/field scenarios where a manager's own judgment needs to be central to the evaluation.
video-coaching.who: Submitted by Learners. Reviewed by Managers. Configured by Editors.

ai-coaching.label: AI Coaching
ai-coaching.tagline: Practice real-world conversations against an AI character that scores you.
ai-coaching.description: The AI-powered coaching module. Learners practice a roleplay (e.g., a sales call with an HCP or customer) against a configurable AI persona, and the AI evaluates and scores the conversation automatically — typically within minutes. Admins can define the AI's role, persona, voice/avatar, difficulty level, and number of allowed attempts. After each session, learners see a feedback screen with their recorded attempt plus a detailed evaluation (strengths, gaps, objection-handling analysis), and managers can still add their own review and feedback on top of the AI's score (blended scoring). Reporting includes attempt-wise and coaching-wise reports, competency/skill dashboards, and team-level improvement tracking — so gaps that show up repeatedly across a learner, a team, or a cohort are easy to spot.
keyFeatures: AI characters with custom personas and scenarios
ai-coaching.who: Practised by Learners. Configured by Editors. Reviewed by Managers.

field-coaching.label: Field Coaching
field-coaching.tagline: Structured ride-along coaching with competency-based scoring.
field-coaching.description: Digitizes the traditional in-field “ride-along,” where a manager accompanies a rep on a real client visit and scores their performance live. Admins build coaching templates that define exactly which competencies get scored, and managers use these templates to evaluate reps during or right after a field visit. It's built around structured, competency-based scoring tied to a real-time, in-person observation, covering live, unscripted, real customer interactions.
keyFeatures: Mobile-first form designed for in-the-field use
Offline support with sync on reconnect
Trend reports by reportee and by competency
field-coaching.who: Conducted by Managers in the field. Configured by Editors.

survey.label: Survey
survey.tagline: Collect structured feedback with templates, sections, and response analytics.
survey.description: The structured feedback-collection module. Editors build surveys or reusable templates using any of eight supported question types, organize questions into sections, and choose how respondents see them — one question at a time, section-by-section, or all at once. Surveys can be assigned to a specific audience or distributed via QR code for anonymous, event-style feedback, with scheduled reminders to boost response rates. Reporting covers both aggregate results (at the survey or template level) and individual response drill-downs, with anonymity settings controlling how much identifying detail is visible.
survey.who: Designed by Editors. Responded to by all Learners.

knowledge-hub.label: Knowledge Hub
knowledge-hub.tagline: A searchable library of reference content for in-the-moment lookup.
knowledge-hub.description: A searchable content repository — the organization's reference library inside SmartWinnr — where editors organize documents and materials (product info, policies, playbooks, etc.) into folders and items. It's built for on-demand lookup: users browse or search recent, trending, and latest items. Editors manage folders/items directly, and usage analytics show what content people are actually going to look up in the field.
keyFeatures: Full-text search from the mobile app
Recent + trending sections on the home tab
Reusable from coaching feedback and AI Coaching
knowledge-hub.who: Curated by Editors. Searched by all Learners.

forms.label: Forms
forms.tagline: Custom data-collection forms with manager approval workflows.
forms.description: A custom data-collection module for structured submissions — field reports, expense claims, activity logs, and similar — with a built-in manager approval workflow. Editors build the form and can add designated approvers; a form can even be submitted on a user's behalf. If approval is required, the submitter only earns points once an approver signs off. Submissions can come from the app, the left menu, or via chat (if the form is shared to a chat group), and managers can review, edit, or approve/reject submissions from their team. Form Analytics gives a rollup view of all submission activity.
keyFeatures: Build custom forms with mixed input types
Submit from the left menu or the chat
Edit submissions from the manager view
forms.who: Submitted by all Learners. Designed by Editors. Approved by Managers.

kpi-gamification.label: KPI & Gamification
kpi-gamification.tagline: Scorecards, competitions, achievements, and engagement leaderboards.
kpi-gamification.description: Turns real organizational performance metrics into a game layer. Admins define KPIs and map them to actual data sources (“Field Mappings”), then build scorecards to measure reps against targets on a daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, or yearly basis. On top of that, admins can run competitions, challenges (individual, group, or manager-led), and brackets to drive engagement around those KPIs, plus award achievements — badges and certificates — on task completion, with leaderboards (individual or team) showing standings during a competition. Detailed KPI reports let managers slice performance by rep, team, or time period.
keyFeatures: KPI scorecards with custom field mapping
kpi-gamification.who: Configured by Editors. Tracked by Managers. Played by all Learners.

notifications.label: Notifications & Chat
notifications.tagline: Custom, scheduled, and triggered notifications plus in-app chat.
notifications.description: Handles automated engagement and communication across the platform. At its core are nudge rules — automated triggers, fired either by an activity event or a schedule, that send a notification/email/in-app action such as assigning a quiz, SmartPath, or survey, or awarding points/badges — targeted at specific users, groups, or attributes. It also covers scheduled reminders for quizzes, surveys, and coaching tasks, and escalation matrices that automatically bump overdue tasks or unanswered queries up the chain of responsibility, so nothing important quietly falls through the cracks.
keyFeatures: Triggered notifications from quiz, coaching, KPI events
notifications.who: Designed by Editors and OrgAdmins. Received by all Learners.

cross-module.label: Cross-Module Features
cross-module.tagline: Behaviour that spans multiple modules — query, app updates, navigation.
cross-module.description: A catch-all for capabilities that cut across every module. This includes shared content tools (attaching images, videos, audio, PDFs, or external links to any activity), platform-wide conveniences like “My Tasks” (a single pending-task list spanning quizzes, surveys, SmartFeeds, coaching, SmartPaths, and forms), QResolve (the in-app query/Q&A system for asking and answering questions), Sales TV, widgets, reminders, and general app navigation and update behavior.
keyFeatures: QResolve — ask the support team a question
SCORM course access from the app
Mobile app updates from the web view
Shared content across competitions and quizzes
cross-module.who: Used by everyone — Learners, Managers, Editors, Admins.

competition.label: Competition
competition.tagline: Gamified challenges scored on learning activities, KPIs, brackets, and leagues.
competition.description: The engagement layer that lets teams or individuals compete against each other using activities from any other module — quizzes, surveys, forms, scorecards, video coaching, SmartFeeds — as the “tasks” being competed on. It supports several formats: standard, bracket-style (paired knockout rounds), video-coaching-level, and activity-progress competitions, each suited to a different use case, plus leaderboards (individual or team) and optional observers who can watch results without taking part themselves.
keyFeatures: LMS-based competitions scored on SmartFeeds, quizzes, surveys, and SmartPaths
Performance-based competitions that rank participants against selected KPIs
Combined competitions pairing learning activities with KPI tracking
Bracket Challenge: tournament rounds from qualifiers to finals on one KPI
League Game: Platinum, Gold, Silver, and Bronze tiers with promotion and relegation
competition.who: Set up by Editors. Open to all Learners, individually or in teams. Leaderboards recognize high-performing users and teams.

authoringtools.label: Authoring Tools
authoringtools.tagline: Create podcasts and audio narrations for your learning content.
authoringtools.description: A newer, AI-assisted content-creation module that helps editors produce learning content faster, without a production studio. It has two components: Video Lab, which turns a slide deck into a narrated training video — upload the PDF, edit the per-slide narration script, choose an AI voice, and generate a video that can be reused elsewhere (e.g., inside a SmartFeed) — and Question Studio (also called Quiz Master), which uses AI to draft quiz questions straight from uploaded source documents, then routes them through a human review queue (approve, edit, reject, or tag) before they're published into the Question Bank for use in quizzes.
